anti_overlap: Covers multi-connector composition; fd-go-python-subprocess-bridge covers transport; fd-query-template-protocol-design covers single-template design
decision_lens: When a query joins data from multiple connectors and one fails, does the result accurately communicate what succeeded and what is missing?
focus: Partial result semantics when multi-connector queries encounter failures
name: fd-cross-connector-fan-out-reliability
persona: Distributed systems engineer who has built federated query engines with heterogeneous data sources
review_areas: Partial result marking: result includes which connectors contributed vs which failed
Empty result vs connector-unavailable distinction (no actors found vs cass down)
Sequential vs parallel connector fan-out and latency implications
Stale data handling: query uses cached crosswalk data when connector harvest is outdated
Error propagation: connector errors bubble up as structured query errors, not silent empty results
Timeout per connector vs global query timeout

severity_examples.condition: cass connector fails but beads data returns successfully, agent treats as complete
severity_examples.scenario: bead_context returns partial data without marking it incomplete

severity_examples.condition: who_touched_file returns zero actors because harvest never ran, not because no one touched the file
severity_examples.scenario: Empty actors list is indistinguishable from never-harvested

severity_examples.condition: 3 connectors each take 1s, total is 3s instead of ~1s with parallel execution

success_hints: QueryResult has explicit connector_status field. Partial results are clearly marked. Fan-out is parallel where possible.
task_context: Multi-connector queries are the core value of interweave. If agents can't distinguish partial from complete results, they make wrong decisions.
